You can also argue that the Indian fast bowlers missed a trick or two as they were unable to hit the ideal length for this pitch consistently enough. They were a bit too short and wide which gave the English southpaws that much extra time to react to any movement and survive the initial difficult phase when the ball was moving.
Better from JB who keeps it fuller on the off stump line. Ali comes forward and defends. THAT'S LUNCH!

That's a Peach! Bumrah extracting some movement and these are encouraging signs for the visiting pacers. Lands this one around off, angling into Ali. The ball hits the deck and deviates away. The movement is enough for the ball to beat Ali's tentative push. Bumrah has his hands on his head. Ali survives a scare.
Similar ball, similar response from Ali, a leave.
Bumrah lands it fuller outside off, Ali patiently lets it go.
Similar length but a much better line, around the off pole. Cook leans across and flicks it wristily towards mid-wicket and runs across for a single.
Bumrah keeps it fuller of a good length but wide of off allowing Cook to have a good look at it and shoulder arms.
Fuller outside off, Moeen makes another leave. A maiden.
Outside off, left alone.
Very full this time, maybe trying to bowl a yorker after the bumper but he misses by quite a lot. Moeen blocks it out.
Excellent bumper there! Good pace and a well-directed one. Moeen, at the last moment, ducks under it. Pant collects it one-handed.
On middle, Moeen works it to mid-wicket.
On the shorter side, Ali does have problems facing the short ball but the line is outside off. He lets it go.
On off, Cook pushes it to covers.
Attacks the off pole now, AC goes back and keeps it out.
A little too straight by Bumrah. Cook off the back foot, flicks it through backward square leg for a brace.
Angles it into the pads, Ali works it through square leg and gets to the other end.
On the stumps this time, Moeen gets behind the line and keeps it out.
Lovely start! He bowls it on off and gets it to move away. Ali pokes at it and gets beaten.
Jasprit Bumrah is back on.
Back of a length on off, kept out.
Tucks it with the angle to mid-wicket.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Nice shot! Shami changes the angle and bowls it very full on off, Cook strokes it down the ground for a brace.
On a length and around off, the batsman blocks it out.
Very wide outside off, Cook lets it go through.
Jadeja marginally pulls the length back and lands this one on off, Ali turns it towards the leg side with the spin.
Nice use of the wrists by the retiring left-hander. Jadeja keeps it fuller on the stumps, Cook leans and flicks it into the mid-wicket region for a single.
A bit flatter and shorter in length from Jaddu. Cook defends from within the crease.
Similar delivery to the last one but this time Ali flicks it wide of mid on to get a single and get off the mark.
A bit tossed up, fuller on the stumps. Ali flicks it to the mid-wicket region.
Moeen Ali is the new man in.

OUT! India draw first blood and totally against the run of play! Jadeja announces his return with a bang. Lands this one on a tighter line attacking the stumps. Jennings attempts to nudge the ball off his pads, through the leg side. The ball spins, kisses the bat face and flies to the leg slip region. Rahul positioned there takes a sharp catch. The tourists are ecstatic. Jennings, while walking back, is seen thumping his bat with his gloves in frustration. He got through the difficult phase but fails to capitalize on the start he got.
Fuller on off, Cook blocks it out off the front foot.
Shami strays this down the leg side. Cook tries to flick it but misses. The tourists appeal as they feel there was some bat on it. The umpire stays unmoved. Replays are inconclusive.
Shami pulls the length back, the experienced England opener defends it from within the crease.
Cook shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Lands this one a bit fuller and just outside off. Cook leans across and defends off the front foot.
Lands it fractionally shorter of a good length around off, Cooks keeps it out off the back foot.
Fuller ball on the stumps, flicked to mid-wicket.

LUCKY, VERY LUCKY! Jadeja tosses this one a bit and keeps it full around off. Keaton skips down the track and tries to play a lofted flick over the mid-wicket region. The ball pitches and skids through to take the top edge and flies towards the cover region. The fielder at mid off runs towards the ball to catch it but cannot reach it. The batsmen. Much better from Jadeja.
Flatter and fuller on off, KJ comes forward and defends.
Again on the pads, flicked straight to mid-wicket.
Fires it on the stumps. Worked towards mid-wicket with the spin.

The left-handed spinner starts off a new over with a flatter delivery on Cook's pads. The English opener will accept such delivery all his life, now that he's retiring after this game. He flicks it towards the square leg region for a single.
A dot to end! Just a single from it. On a length around off, Jennings tries to defend but gets an inside edge towards mid-wicket.
A bumper but the line is outside off, KJ watches it go through to the keeper.
Wide outside off, Jennings opts not to play at it.
Tucks it around the corner with the angle for a run.
On a length again, this time it comes back in with the angle. Also skids through after pitching. Cook tries to keep it out but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Good length outside off, left alone.
A bit flatter and shorter by Jaddu. Jennings gets behind the line of the delivery and blocks it out.
Similar delivery to the last one, but this one is pushed a bit far from the fielder at mid on. The batsmen exchange strike.
Lands this one a bit straight attacking the stumps, Cook gets across the line and turns it away into the mid-wicket region. No run on offer there.
Tosses this up around off, Cook defends off the front foot.

Appeal for an LBW, but turned down. Jadeja fires this one a bit shorter of full length outside off, the ball pitches and turns in sharply. Cook, looking to play the sweep shot, misses the ball and gets hit on his pads. The Indians appeal but the umpire immediately turns it down as the impact was outside off.
Cook has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Much better from Shami to end the over. Lands this one fuller around off. Jennings trying to push at the ball, gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Shami, in trying to suck the batsman into a drive, lands this very full and wide of off. Jennings squeezes this one into the cover region and gets a single for it.
Pulls the length back and keeps it on the stumps. KJ gets right behind the ball and keeps it out.
Lands this one abit shorter of good length outside off. Keaton shoulders arms.
Keeps it full just outside off. Looks like KJ has got his eye in now as he leans and creams this drive through the cover region to pick up a brace.
Starts the new over with a length ball outside off. Jennings leaves it alone.
Strays on his pads again, Keaton has nudged the ball fine down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Jadeja gets a bit too straight and fires this one on the batsman's pads. Keaton drives this to mid-wicket to pick up a quick single.
KJ blocks this delivery off the front foot into the ground.

A bit wide of off, Cook plays it off the front foot into the point region. One run added to the total. This also brings up the 50-run stand up between the English openers. They have really showed grit and played it out really well.
Fuller on middle and leg, pushed through the mid-wicket region.
Strays it down the leg side. Cooks tries to flick but misses as Pant collects it.
Very full and it tails back in. Jennings covers it and works it to mid on for a run.
On a length and around off, Jennings makes a leave.
On the shorter side outside off, Jennings goes for the cut but gets a bottom edge to point.
Length again on off, KJ is solid in defense.
On a length and around off, coming back in. Jennings defends it.
Length again on off, it pitches and comes back in a touch. Cook tries to block but the ball goes off the inner half towards square leg for a run.

FOUR! Reverse Broomed! Second four of the over but this time off the bat. Jadeja fires this one quicker and very full on off. Keaton premeditates, goes down and plays a wonderful reverse sweep, much to the surprise of everyone. His connection is near perfect as the ball flies past the backward point region for a cracking boundary.
A bit fuller this time in the off stump area. KJ keeps it out off the front foot.

Much better by the left handed spinner. He bowls this a bit slower and on the middle stump line. Jennings, looking to defend off the front foot, is beaten by the spin and the ball strikes him very low on the pads The touring team is asking the question but the umpire shows no interest in the appeal.
Fires this flatter one on his pads, Cook works it down with the angle into the square leg region and gets a single for it.
FOUR Byes! Strays down on his second ball and concedes four byes. Pant won't be happy as this one was way quicker and down the leg. The keeper tried his best to stop it but could not.
Jadeja starts off with a flatter delivery on the stumps. Cooks comes forward and defends.
Ravindra Jadeja comes into the attack.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
Good length again on off, Cook defends it.
On the shorter side and width is on offer outside off, Cook punches it through point and runs two.
On a length around off, Cook defends it.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
EDGED AND FOUR! Shami starts off with a very good delivery, on off and straightening a touch. Cook plays inside the line, the ball takes the outside edge and goes to the third man fence.
Mohammad Shami comes into the attack.

That's the first drinks break of the final match of the series. England have had the perfect start. They have reached 32 without losing any wickets. The Indian pacers have tried hard, keeping the ball in good areas. However, they have not been able to extract too much from the wicket and this has made life easier for the English openers. Can India strike after the break? Or will England continue their procession?
Very full again on middle, Keaton drives it to mid on. A tight over to begin with by Vihari.
Tries to toss this one up but ends up bowling a full toss. Jennings strokes it to covers.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fires it on off, KJ blocks it out. He is bowling it too quick, needs to slow it up a touch.
Drift! A lot of it into the batsman. Also it is bowled quicker. Jennings goes back and keeps it out.
Starts off with a flatter delivery outside off, Cook punches it through covers and takes a run.
Hanuma Vihari, the debutant, is into the attack. A surprise move by Virat Kohli. Not a lot of people would have expected him to bowl at this stage. Can he deliver the goods?
FOUR! Easy-peasy! Signs of Bumrah tiring? Maybe. He bowls this on the pads, Jennings flicks it fine down the leg side for his first boundary of his innings.
A little too wide outside off, left alone.
Driven towards the mid on region.

Nicely bowled! Not a lot you can do about that as a batsman. Bumrah first draws Jennings into a stroke as he angles it into the batsman. It pitches and then leaves Jennings late. Beating the outside edge.
Good length again on off, KJ plants his front foot forward and pushes it to covers.
Bowls it on a fuller length on off, Jennings prods forward and blocks it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Fuller in length on off, shaping away from Cook, late. Alastair goes for the drive but the ball takes the outside edge and goes towards backward point.
Hits the length hard on off, Cook off the back foot keeps it out.
On a length outside off, Cook away from his body has a feel for it as he plays it to point.
The line this time would not have impressed the Windies great as it is on the pads. Jennings flicks it through square leg. There is protection in the deep so, only a run results.
On the 5th stump channel! Also on a length which impresses Michael Holding in the commentary box. Jennings plays it towards point.
A single to end the over! Good length on off, KJ taps it towards covers and takes a brisk run.
Length again outside off, the batsman need not play at those.
Fuller in length on off, Jennings pushes it back to the bowler.
Good length on off, it comes on to the bat quite nicely and KJ defends it.
Good length on off, Jennings is half-forward as he keeps it out.
Bumrah, who is into his sixth over, bowls it just behind a length outside off, left alone.
Bowls it on a length around off, Cook blocks it out.

Bang! Right on the grille! I feel Jennings misjudged the length there. It was short but not very short. Certainly not a ball which you should be ducking on a slow wicket. Jennings does so by taking the eyes off the ball. He is hit right on the helmet as the ball rolls towards square leg. The batsmen run a leg bye. Takes his helmet off after getting to the other end and signals to the dressing room that he is fine.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Outswing but the line is wrong, outside off. Jennings is not interested at playing at those.
On the stumps, Keaton works it to mid-wicket.
Decent carry for Ishant but the line is way too wide outside off, Keaton shoulders arms to it.
Bumrah changes his length again and pulls it a bit behind good length, around off, the England opener goes back and blocks it under his eyes.
Lands this a bit fuller but wide of off. Cook has nothing to do with this one as he shoulders arms.
Length ball attacking the stumps, defended off the back foot by Cook.

FOUR! One more excellent shot by England's most capped player. Bumrah tries to surprise the batsman with a short ball. But Cook is aware enough to sight the length early, go back, swivel and play the perfect pull shot through square leg. The ball races across the deep square leg boundary.

FOUR! Cook at his best here. How many times have we seen this from the great opener? JB lands this a bit short and wide of off. Cook rocks back and unleashes a Cook special square cut. The timing and placement is exquisite as the ball runs through to the point boundary.
Bumrah starts a new over from around the wicket, lands this fractionally fuller than a good length, just wide of off and angling into Cook. The left hander leaves it watchfully.
On the shorter side, KJ stays inside the crease and blocks it.
On off, KJ blocks it out.
Back of a length on off, Keaton with soft hands plays it to gully.
Just ahead of a length around off, Jennings first thinks of playing at it but then looking at the away movement, lets it be.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Good length around off, Jennings guides it to point.
Full again on off, Jennings strokes it through mid off and keeps the strike for the next over.
Outside off, not a lot of carry. KJ lets it be.
Back of a length outside off, Jennings opts not to play at it.
Good length on middle, Jennings pushes it to mid on.
Shortish in length and outside off, Cook stands tall, gets on top of the bounce and punches it through covers for a run.
Fullish on off, Jennings punches it down towards mid off, waits for the ball to cross the bowler and takes a run after that.
Again bowls a tight line on off, Cook is solid in defense.
On off, defended.
Hits the length hard and bowls it on off, Cook gets behind the line and defends it.
The ball is down the leg side but the batsman still goes after it.
Leading edge... but safe! On middle angling into the batsman. It pitches and straightens. Cook tries to flick it but the ball takes a soft leading edge.
Excellent start to the over! Ishant finds some movement and bowls it full and on off. It shapes away at the very last moment, beating the outside edge of Cook's bat.

OHHH! The sucker ball almost does the trick. Smart change in length there by JB. He goes full after continuously bowling length. It is also wide outside off, tempting the batsman to go for a loose shot. He is successful as Keaton goes after it with no foot movement but luckily for him, gets beaten.
On the shorter side, not a lot of bounce from the wicket as Jennings tucks it off his hips towards mid-wicket.
Bumrah gets this one to shape back in just a touch from outside off, Jennings watchfully makes the third leave of the over.
Outside off this time, left alone.
Down the leg side, Jennings watches it go through to the keeper.
Slightly too straight by Bumrah, Jennings tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. He might feel he missed out there on a scoring opportunity.

Finishes the over with a good nut! On off and straightening a touch. Cook gets squared up a little as he defends it to covers. So no real seam or swing on offer for the bowlers, looks a real good batting deck from what we have seen now.
Bowls it wide outside off, Cook need not play at those.
Again Ishant angles it into the pads of the batsman. Shorter in length this time. Cook works it to mid-wicket.
FOUR! First boundary of the innings! Bread and butter stuff for Cook, on his pads. He says thank you very much, flicks it through square leg and bags a boundary.
Angles it into the batsman, Cook with the angle tucks it to mid-wicket.
Attacks the off stump from around the wicket. Looking to swing it away after angling in. The movement which has troubled the left-handers throughout, however, Cook blocks it with ease.
Bumrah misses his line and strays down the leg side, KJ tries to get bat on ball but is unable to do so and the ball is pouched by Pant behind.
Similar delivery to the last one, this time Cook punches it off the back foot into the cover region to add another run to the total.
Keeps it a fractionally behind the good length area, on middle and off. Jennings stays within the crease and taps it towards the point region to pick up a quick single.

Bumrah continues in that corridor around the off stump, Jennings, initially looking to play at it, pulls his bat near his body at the last moment as the ball whizzes past the outside edge into Pant's gloves.
A bit shorter of a length on off, Jennings gets right behind the ball and defends.

Starts from over the wicket with a length ball on leg stump, angling away from KJ. The ball lands and moves away considerably, squaring up Jennings in the process as he gets rapped on his thigh pad. Bumrah getting the ball to talk now.
Good length again on off, Cook shuffles across to his off pole and defends it off the back foot.
Back of a length on off, Cook defends it onto the ground.

Keaton now gets off the mark! Ishant once again goes full, searching for the outswing he has been getting throughout the series. There ain't any. Jennings strokes it through covers. Jadeja runs after it from point, slides and saves a run for his side. This is what the left-arm spinner adds to the team, not only can he bat and bowl but he is an exceptional fielder as well.
On the off stump, no movement for Ishant. Jennings easily blocks it out.
Off the mark is Cook in his final Test and he does so with a classic cover drive. Full and on off, he leans into it and times it through covers for three.
A loosener to start with by Ishant! Full and way too wide outside off, so wide that it would have been signaled one in an ODI. Cook shoulders arms to it.
Ishant Sharma to bowl from the other end.

BYE! England are underway, courtesy an extra. Bumrah once again sprays it down the leg side, Cook lets it be and Pant dives full stretch to his right but fails to hang on. It rolls towards fine leg and the batsmen run a bye.
Gets back to attacking the stumps and bowls it around off, Cook gets behind the line and keeps it out. First ball to hit the bat today.
Good take by Pant! He bowls it down the leg side, Cook misses the flick and Rishabh dives to his right and stops it. Erred in line there Bumrah.

Almost an action replay of the last delivery! Excellent start by Bumrah. He once again bowls it on off, on a back of a length. Makes good use of the angle as he slants it across the batsman. Cook pokes at it and gets beaten. Good carry also as Pant collects it head height.

BEATEN! Excellent second delivery, it is almost similar to the last one. This time it is a touch fuller and closer to the off. It pitches and angles away from Cook. He has to play at it due to the original trajectory but is beaten by the away angle.

Starts off with a length slightly on the shorter side, not giving the ball a lot of chance to move and hence, no movement seen on the first delivery. It slants across the batsman from the off pole. Cook covers his off pole and makes a leave.

We are all set to get underway... out come the Indian players along with the umpires. They are followed by the English openers, Alastair Cook, who is playing his last Test and Keaton Jennings, who needs to get his career kick-started with some runs in this game. The former will be on strike and he will face Jasprit Bumrah. He has three slips and a gully in place. Here we go...

India's captain Virat Kohli says, he would want a coin with heads on both sides if he wants to win a toss. Adds further that the wicket looks good at first sight and feels it has a bit more grass than the one at Southampton. Expects that there will be some help for the bowlers early on. Informs that Hardik Pandya makes way for Hanuma Vihari and R Ashwin is replaced by Ravindra Jadeja. Talking about Cook, says that sometimes they have had too much of him. Ends by saying that he is a great great player, has played more than 160 Tests and will go down as one of the greatest openers to have played the game.

England's captain Joe Root says, that the pitch looks difficult to read. Adds further that it looks like it is a bit dry underneath and hence, the two spinners will come into play later in the game.  Reckons that they will have to wait and see if this wicket is similar to the one at Southampton but states that it should be good for batting from the afternoon period. About his former captain, Alastair Cook, mentions that they have had some memorable games together and have enjoyed battling it out for the team. Ends by saying that they will want to give him a perfect send off by winning this match.
TOSS - Up goes the coin and it lands in the favor of the home side. Five out of five for Joe Root as he elects to bat first.

Pitch Report - Sanjay Manjrekar says that the pitch looks similar to the Wankhede stadium pitch in Mumbai. Adds further, that the deck has a decent covering of grass. Feels that because the batting for both sides has not done well this series, the captain who wins the toss may elect to bowl first to put pressure on the opposition batters early on. Reckons, this pitch will do something for the first couple of hours. Also expects it to dry up as the game progresses.

It is time for the final encounter of this extremely exciting and entertaining series. A Dead rubber? Not sure England or India will look at this game in that manner. It is a chance for the home side to further establish their dominance over the visitors in home conditions. Whereas, the away side will want to end the tour on a high. Changes in the XI? Well, we do expect a few from the Indian side. Who comes in? How will the pitch play in this game? The pitch report and all information from the toss will be available in a bit. Stay tuned.
